critical_steps: Both swapped coordinate families are Parseval g-frames and are K-g-frames with lower bound 16 for K=I/4.
For alpha=beta=mu=3/4, the printed scalar threshold is 9/4<4.
The adjoint perturbation norm is sqrt(2) times the coefficient norm, while the printed right side is 9/4 times that norm.
The weave selecting Lambda_1 and Gamma_2 consists twice of the e1 coordinate and has zero energy on e2.
Because K is invertible, K*e2 is nonzero, so that weave cannot satisfy any positive lower K-g-frame inequality.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact two-dimensional scalar Hilbert-module counterexample satisfying every displayed hypothesis of Theorem 3.10.
integrity.unproved_limits: No necessary-and-sufficient replacement perturbation criterion is claimed.

scientific_limitations: The finding refutes Theorem 3.10 as printed and identifies its non-scale-invariant K-dependence.
No complete replacement perturbation theorem for arbitrary Hilbert C*-modules is asserted.
An unindexed erratum, thesis remark, or informal correction may contain the same observation.
title: A \(K\)-rescaling counterexample to a woven \(K\)-\(g\)-frame perturbation theorem
